title: EMFI | Home
description: Institutional infrastructure. Without the institutional layers. Research, execution, settlement, custody and asset management for professional clients.

items.label: Cost
items.heading: Look beyond the headline rate.
items.body: Fewer intermediaries taking their markup. More of your money stays where it belongs.
items.detail: Compare custody charges, transaction fees, annual minimums and processing costs on a like-for-like basis. A more direct structure may remove some charges, but savings depend on the services, markets and assets involved.
items.note: Fees should be compared on the same assets, markets, service scope and activity levels.

items.label: Complexity
items.heading: Fewer parties. Clearer responsibilities.
items.body: More operational control. Faster answers, fewer delays and smoother execution.
items.detail: Each additional party can bring another agreement, instruction path, reconciliation and escalation. Fewer relationships can simplify coordination and make responsibility easier to trace, where the operating model permits.
points: How many agreements govern the chain?
items.note: The actual operating model varies by market, instrument and service.

items.label: Exposure
items.heading: Know who holds your assets.
items.body: Fewer points of failure. Simpler asset tracing and recovery if an intermediary defaults.
items.detail: Every asset-holding intermediary can introduce another counterparty dependency. If one fails, access to, reconciliation of or recovery of assets may be delayed or disputed. A shorter chain can reduce third-party dependencies, but it does not automatically make custody safer.
points: What happens if an intermediary fails?
What ownership and recovery rights apply?
items.note: Risk depends on legal ownership, segregation, account structure, insolvency protections and contractual rights.
